description: Ale, ancestors and frost - a barbarian who makes the whole warband hit harder.
_source_note: Rebuilt 6 Nov 2026 from the 42 real CoA Ancestry talents (role SUPPORT), the largest Barbarian spec and the thinnest tree in the project at 3 procs. CoA writes nine of its talents as party auras and eight such abilities ALREADY exist as target_type 'party' - Barbarian was authored properly on the ability side, like Ranger - so the talents modify those auras instead of trying to be them. Barbarian summons, so pet keys are legal, but pets never fire procs. The Tankard's Fill Level stacks do not exist, which costs seven talents. Last tree of the CoA rebuild.

nodes.name: Trip to the Alehouse
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Keg Smash by 20% and your area damage by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases the damage of Keg Smash by 10% and its range by 3 yds.' The damage ports (doubled); range is not a mechanic here. Replaced with aoe_damage, which IS live and is read at abilities.py:1600 only when target_type is enemy_aoe - so it is genuinely scoped to area attacks, and Keg Smash is one of five this spec has. Both FRACTIONS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Drinking Frenzy
nodes.description: Increases your hit chance by 5% and your pets' damage by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your melee attacks now have a 15% chance to grant a stack of Fill Level. In addition, your chance to hit is increased by 5%.' The hit chance ports verbatim. CoA scales this off FILL LEVEL, the Tankard's stack mechanic. Barbarian is (ResourceType.ENERGY, None) with no secondary pool, and nothing reads a stack count anyway, so there is nothing to count. Seven Ancestry talents depend on it; each is flattened to its unconditional form. Same situation as Chronomancer's Echo Fragments and Venomancer's Brood Marks - and the reason CHECK THE RESOURCE FIRST is a standing rule, since Templar's Combo, Reaper's Souls and Ranger's Focus all turned out to be real. Replaced with pet damage, which is the tree's other theme. hit_rating is live as a FLAT bonus in PERCENTAGE POINTS - it is only invalid as a CONVERSION target, which with stamina has cost ten nodes half their text across eight classes. pet_damage is a FRACTION. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Uniting Voice
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of Ancestral Roar and Warband by 35% and increases Ancestral Roar's healing by 25%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Ancestral Roar now increases haste of party and raid members by 5% for 20 sec. Does not stack with similar effects. Critical strikes extend the duration of the buff by 1 sec.' THE PARTY HASTE IS REAL BUT NOT FROM A TALENT - a talent effect can never reach an ally. barbarian_ancestral_fury and barbarian_warband already carry party haste and healing as target_type 'party' ABILITIES (abilities.py:2064 resolves 'party' to all living allies), so this talent does what a talent can: make them available more often. The extend-on-crit clause cannot be built either - no payload extends a LIVE effect's duration. Ancestral Roar is effect_type heal, so its buff takes ability_<id>_HEALING; _damage on a heal does nothing while passing every check. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Frost Giant's Fury
nodes.description: Increases your Frost damage by 12% and your haste by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Breath of the North now grants you 10% melee attack speed, plus an additional 20% when using a two-handed weapon, for 8 sec.' The haste ports as a passive: there is no per-ability proc trigger, and the two-handed clause cannot be built because nothing reads weapon type (which also cost Thane's Grip, Thane's Guard and eleven Felsworn Slayer talents their conditions). Folded in CoA's Ancestor's Fury ('Unbridled Rage now also increases your Frost damage by 10%'), whose trigger fails the same way. frost_spell_damage IS LIVE - built via an f-string at abilities.py:1371 inside _school_damage_bonus and resolved against the ability's real school, so a literal grep cannot see it; this spec has three frost abilities (Hodir's Wrath, Breath of the North, Frozen Tankard). A FRACTION; haste is PERCENTAGE POINTS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Ancestral Wisdom
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of your party auras by 35%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases chance to hit with all spells and attacks by 1% for you and party and raid members. Does not stack with similar effects.' A TALENT EFFECT CAN NEVER REACH AN ALLY, and unlike Guardian, Reaper, Necromancer and Felsworn there was nothing to convert here - all eight of Barbarian's aura abilities were ALREADY target_type 'party'. So rather than build a selfish shadow of CoA's aura, this node makes four of those real auras available far more often, which is a thing only a talent can do. That is the same solution Ranger Farstrider's Blow the Horns! uses, and it makes the tree MORE faithful than forcing aura effects into talent slots would. FRACTIONS where POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION; talented_cooldown floors at 1 turn.

nodes.name: Icebound Ancestry
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of your Frost abilities by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the critical strike chance of Breath of the North by 10%. In addition, your attacks now ignore Armor against Frozen targets.' The crit ports (raised to 15%) and is extended to the spec's other two frost abilities. The armour clause fails twice: nothing reads a target's debuffs, so 'against Frozen targets' is unreachable, and armor_penetration is FLAT rather than proportional so 'ignore Armor' has no all-or-nothing form. CoA's Hodir's Revenge gates on Frozen the same way. Per-ability crit keys are PERCENTAGE POINTS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Cold Brew
nodes.description: Your critical strikes restore 12 Energy.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Critical strikes with Frost damage now generate a stack of Fill Level. Can only occur once per sec.' CoA scales this off FILL LEVEL, the Tankard's stack mechanic. Barbarian is (ResourceType.ENERGY, None) with no secondary pool, and nothing reads a stack count anyway, so there is nothing to count. Seven Ancestry talents depend on it; each is flattened to its unconditional form. Same situation as Chronomancer's Echo Fragments and Venomancer's Brood Marks - and the reason CHECK THE RESOURCE FIRST is a standing rule, since Templar's Combo, Reaper's Souls and Ranger's Focus all turned out to be real. Re-pointed to the pool that DOES exist - Energy, Barbarian's single primary resource - so the node keeps its shape (crit, get resource) through a mechanic that works. The Frost scoping goes: there is no per-school proc filter, since proc['school'] only TYPES a damage_flat payload. grant_resource routes through the same gain_resource() the class's three generators use, so the cap holds, and its `amount` is FLAT.

nodes.name: The Spins
nodes.description: Increases your pets' damage by a further 30% and their health by 25%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Keg Smash now causes your Honored Ancestor to perform an Ancestral Whirl attack upon nearby enemies.' Barbarian genuinely summons - barbarian_ancestors_call is a real summon_pet ability - so pet_damage/pet_health/pet_armor are legal keys here, which tools/qa_pet_keys.py exists to police after Witch Doctor Shadow Hunting shipped three on a class that summons nothing. But PETS NEVER FIRE PROCS (no fire_proc_trigger anywhere in entities/pet.py), nothing reads a live pet count, and no proc can apply an effect to a pet, so the Honored Ancestor's own behaviour cannot be changed - only its scaling. So an ancestor that mimics your abilities cannot be built, and the node becomes flat pet scaling - the same intent (your ancestor matters more) through the only keys that reach it. Folded in CoA's Drunken Frenzy ('Unbridled Rage now increases your Honored Ancestor's Physical damage by 15%') and Ale of The God-King's empowerment, both of which fail the same way. Both FRACTIONS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Liquid Courage
nodes.description: Reduces all damage you take by 6% and increases your maximum health by 8%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Each Fill Level stack now reduces your damage taken by -2%.' CoA scales this off FILL LEVEL, the Tankard's stack mechanic. Barbarian is (ResourceType.ENERGY, None) with no secondary pool, and nothing reads a stack count anyway, so there is nothing to count. Seven Ancestry talents depend on it; each is flattened to its unconditional form. Same situation as Chronomancer's Echo Fragments and Venomancer's Brood Marks - and the reason CHECK THE RESOURCE FIRST is a standing rule, since Templar's Combo, Reaper's Souls and Ranger's Focus all turned out to be real. Built as the flat mitigation CoA's typical three stacks would give, plus health so the node is worth a point on a support spec. BOTH KEYS ARE FRACTIONS AS TALENT EFFECTS: damage_taken_pct is read RAW (character.py:2696), so -0.06 is -6%, and max_health_pct is a fraction here but PERCENTAGE POINTS inside a status effect - the same key, two conventions, depending on where it is written. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Blind Stupor
nodes.description: Your attacks have a 35% chance to daze the target, weakening their attacks for 4 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage dealt by Keg Smash now reduces enemies' casting speed by 30% for 15 sec.' THERE IS NO CASTER-SIDE SPEED DEBUFF KEY - that gap has now cost nodes on five classes, including Chronomancer's Destabilize Time, whose entire mechanic it was - so this becomes a flat attack power reduction, which weakens the target's output the way a slower cast would. attack_power is one of only eight status stat_mods a monster reads and it is FLAT (Monster.ability_power_bonus: 'Flat damage/healing swing from active buffs and debuffs'). The Keg Smash scoping goes (no per-ability proc trigger). 15 sec -> 4 turns.

nodes.name: Frostbite
nodes.description: Your Frost damage has a 35% chance to freeze the target, dealing damage over 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Breath of The North now causes the target to bleed for an additional 30% of its damage over 6 sec as Frost damage.' The dot ports; the Breath-of-the-North scoping does not (no per-ability proc trigger), and '30% of its damage' becomes a fixed potency because apply_effect cannot read the triggering hit's amount - only bonus_pct, leech_pct and smart heals do, and none of them apply an effect. The description says 'your Frost damage' loosely: proc['school'] is NOT a trigger-side filter, it only types a damage_flat payload, so this fires on any damaging cast. 6 sec -> 3 turns. A proc-applied dot carries `potency` as PER-TURN damage (26 a turn, 78 total).

nodes.name: Unified Rage
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of Unbridled Rage and Ancestral Combat by 35% and increases your physical damage by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Unbridled Rage now increases your chance to trigger Ancestral Combat by 25%.' Ancestral Combat is a self-buff in our data rather than a proc, so there is no trigger chance to raise - and nothing reads whether Unbridled Rage is active anyway. Rebuilt as cooldown reductions on both named abilities plus a small global. Folded in CoA's Improved Ancestral Combat ('reduces the Energy cost by -10 and allows it to trigger 3 additional times'), whose second clause needs a use counter: nothing counts how many times an effect has fired. FRACTIONS where POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION, beside a fraction that adds - the two sign conventions sit in one dict. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Ramhorn Rage
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of Ramhorn Rage and Warband by 40% and increases their healing by 25%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Enrage party and raid members within 8 yds for 3 sec, regenerating 2% of their maximum health every 1.5 sec. Melee auto attacks extend the duration of this effect by 2 sec, up to a maximum of 15 sec. This ability empties your Tankard.' Both abilities already exist as target_type 'party' HOTs, so THE PARTY HEALING IS REAL - it just cannot come from a talent. The extend-on-auto-attack clause cannot be built (no payload extends a LIVE effect's duration) and CoA scales this off FILL LEVEL, the Tankard's stack mechanic. Barbarian is (ResourceType.ENERGY, None) with no secondary pool, and nothing reads a stack count anyway, so there is nothing to count. Seven Ancestry talents depend on it; each is flattened to its unconditional form. Same situation as Chronomancer's Echo Fragments and Venomancer's Brood Marks - and the reason CHECK THE RESOURCE FIRST is a standing rule, since Templar's Combo, Reaper's Souls and Ranger's Focus all turned out to be real. So this talent makes two real party heal-over-times stronger and far more frequent. BOTH TAKE ability_<id>_HEALING, not _damage: they are HOTs, and _damage on a heal passes every check while doing nothing.

nodes.name: War Cry
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of War Cry and Tavern Brawl by 40% and increases your attack power by 8%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Unleash a blood curdling war cry, increasing melee and ranged attack speed by 20%, and attack power by 150 of party and raid members within 25 yds for 20 sec. Allies cannot benefit from this spell again for 5 min.' Both abilities exist as target_type 'party' buffs, so the party effect is real and this talent shortens their cooldowns. The 5-minute exhaustion lockout has no mechanism - nothing prevents a buff being reapplied to the same target - which also cost Ranger's Frenzy and Command Aura their drawbacks, so this is a case where losing CoA's restriction is a straight gain and is flagged rather than pocketed quietly. attack_power_pct is PERCENTAGE POINTS, which audit_talents caught me authoring as a fraction on Ranger Brigand tonight.

nodes.name: Crystal Enhancements
nodes.description: Increases your armor by 18% and reduces the cooldown of Clanlord's Totem and Frozen Blades by 30%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'You now emanate an aura around you, increasing the Armor of party and raid members by 390. Does not stack with similar effects.' A talent effect can never reach an ally, and there is no Barbarian 'Crystal Enhancements' ABILITY to convert - but clanlords_totem and frozen_blades ARE party abilities, so the node takes CoA's armour selfishly and makes those two available more often. KEPT UNDER THE CAP DELIBERATELY: check_talent_balance enforces an armor_pct ceiling of 60 and Venomancer Fortitude currently breaches it at 62 from two stacking nodes, so this tree carries exactly one armour node. armor_pct is PERCENTAGE POINTS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Ice Cold Bubbles
nodes.description: Increases your Frost damage by a further 10% and the damage of Frozen Tankard by 30%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Each Fill Level stack now also increases Frost damage dealt by 2%.' CoA scales this off FILL LEVEL, the Tankard's stack mechanic. Barbarian is (ResourceType.ENERGY, None) with no secondary pool, and nothing reads a stack count anyway, so there is nothing to count. Seven Ancestry talents depend on it; each is flattened to its unconditional form. Same situation as Chronomancer's Echo Fragments and Venomancer's Brood Marks - and the reason CHECK THE RESOURCE FIRST is a standing rule, since Templar's Combo, Reaper's Souls and Ranger's Focus all turned out to be real. Built as the flat value CoA's typical five stacks would give, plus damage on Frozen Tankard, which no other node touches. Stacks with Frost Giant's Fury and the Frost theme generally. frost_spell_damage is live via an f-string lookup; both keys are FRACTIONS.

nodes.name: Cheers!
nodes.description: Your healing spells have a 30% chance to mend your most wounded ally.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Designate an ally as your drinking partner for 30 min, reducing all damage they take by 5%, and causing 10% of all damage they take to be redirected to you.' THE REDIRECTION HAS NO MECHANISM - nothing reroutes damage from one combatant to another, which is the same gap that killed Chronomancer's The Vast Infinite and Reaper's Spectral Warden threat transfer - and a talent cannot put a damage-reduction buff on a chosen ally either. The barbarian_cheers ABILITY exists as an ally-targeted buff and carries that half. So the talent does the thing a talent CAN do for allies: smart_heal_pct, one of only three payloads that reach an ally at all, which picks the worst-off one. NOTE on_heal_cast passes the CASTER, never the healed ally, and a HoT fires no on_heal_cast at all - so this keys off the spec's direct heals (Ancestral Roar, Savage Revelry), not Warband or Ramhorn Rage.

nodes.name: Ancestral Combat
nodes.description: Your attacks have a 25% chance to strike an additional time.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Empower yourself, granting your Physical damage dealt a 25% chance to trigger an additional main hand attack as Frost damage on your target and grant a stack of Fill Level. Lasts until triggered 20 times.' THE CORE PORTS VERBATIM, chance included: `extra_attack` is a BOOLEAN giving exactly one extra attack, which is precisely what CoA asks for. Three things do not - 'lasts until triggered 20 times' needs a use counter, the Fill Level stack does not exist, and the extra attack cannot be retyped as Frost (extra_attack carries no school, unlike damage_flat). Built as a passive rather than the 30-second self-buff, since a talent cannot grant a proc-carrying window without a nested proc the audit cannot inspect.

nodes.name: The Finest Ale
nodes.description: Increases the healing of Savage Revelry by 35% and reduces its cooldown by 30%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Ale of The God-King no longer empties your Tankard.' CoA scales this off FILL LEVEL, the Tankard's stack mechanic. Barbarian is (ResourceType.ENERGY, None) with no secondary pool, and nothing reads a stack count anyway, so there is nothing to count. Seven Ancestry talents depend on it; each is flattened to its unconditional form. Same situation as Chronomancer's Echo Fragments and Venomancer's Brood Marks - and the reason CHECK THE RESOURCE FIRST is a standing rule, since Templar's Combo, Reaper's Souls and Ranger's Focus all turned out to be real. With no Tankard to empty, the talent has literally nothing to act on, so it is re-pointed to Savage Revelry - the spec's self-heal, which also generates 20 Energy and had no node. It is effect_type heal, so it takes ability_<id>_HEALING: _damage on a heal passes every check while doing nothing, which is how 18 talents across four classes were silently dead before _healing was accepted. The cooldown key is a FRACTION where POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION.

nodes.name: Ancestral Spirit
nodes.description: Reduces the cost of all your abilities by 20%, increases your pets' damage by a further 35%, and your critical strikes restore 15 Energy.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Reduces the Energy cost of your Spirit spells and increases the duration of your Shouts by -50%.' 'Spirit spells' and 'Shouts' are CoA ability CATEGORIES and the engine has no such concept - there is no ability-group key, which is the same wall 'Spears' hit in Headhunting and 'Command spells' hit across Necromancer - so the cost reduction becomes global, which is what it amounts to on a spec whose whole kit is Spirit spells. The capstone then pays off the tree's two other themes: pet damage stacking with Drinking Frenzy and The Spins to +85%, and a second Energy grant stacking with Cold Brew to 27 per crit. LAST NODE OF THE CoA REBUILD - all 21 classes, 63 trees. all_ability_cost_pct is a FRACTION where POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION; pet_damage is a fraction that adds.
